items.name: The Anthologist
items.description: A Gresham Street bar and restaurant used for business, founder and technology community events.

items.name: London Mithraeum Bloomberg SPACE
items.description: The reconstructed Roman Temple of Mithras and Bloomberg SPACE exhibition beneath Bloomberg’s City of London headquarters.

items.name: Hampstead Heath
items.description: The City of London-managed open space of woods, meadows, bathing facilities and viewpoints beside NW3.

items.name: Golders Hill Park bandstand
items.description: The outdoor bandstand used for the park's free summer concert programme.

items.name: Barbican Conservatory
items.description: The Barbican's rooftop glasshouse, home to around 800 plant species and a programme of free openings and events.

items.name: Horizon 22
items.description: London's highest free viewing platform, on Level 58 of 22 Bishopsgate with 300-degree city views.

items.name: World's End Estate
items.description: A Chelsea housing estate serving as the London place-based test bed for Imperial's AI4URBAN-HEALTH network.

items.name: Wayve headquarters
items.description: The York Way headquarters of the London autonomous-driving company developing the Wayve AI Driver.

items.name: King's College London, Strand Campus
items.description: King's central London campus and a base for the university's mathematics and theoretical-physics research.

items.name: Tower of London
items.description: The historic royal fortress beside the Thames, home to the Crown Jewels and daily opening and closing ceremonies.

items.name: Keats House
items.description: The Regency villa where John Keats lived and wrote, now a City of London museum with a garden and public programme.

items.name: Parliament Hill Bandstand
items.description: The Hampstead Heath bandstand used for the free Parliament Hill summer concert series.

items.name: London Film School
items.description: The film school and short-course venue at 24 Shelton Street in Covent Garden.

items.name: Guildhall
items.description: The City of London’s historic ceremonial and administrative centre beside Guildhall Yard.

items.name: Sainsbury Wellcome Centre
items.description: UCL’s neuroscience research centre on Howland Street and venue for the Neuroinformatics Unit’s open-software school.

items.name: Kenwood
items.description: The free-to-enter English Heritage house and landscaped estate on the northern edge of Hampstead Heath.

items.name: Hampstead Theatre
items.description: A purpose-built theatre beside Swiss Cottage station, known for commissioning and producing new writing.

items.name: Artizan Street Library and Community Centre
items.description: Public library and community centre near Aldgate, with step-free access, books, events and a maker space.

items.name: Barbican Library
items.description: Public library on Level 2 of the Barbican Centre, with adult, children’s and music collections and a Bostock Room used for events.

items.name: Burgh House and Hampstead Museum
items.description: Historic house and Hampstead museum in New End Square; meeting point for local guided walks.

items.name: The Hill Garden and Pergola
items.description: Public landscaped garden and historic Pergola on the western side of Hampstead Heath. Seasonal hours and maintenance restrictions apply.

items.name: Highgate Wood
items.description: Ancient public woodland managed by the City of London, with wildlife, café, information hut and guided walks.

items.name: Keats Community Library
items.description: Community library next door to Keats House on Keats Grove, with a domed building and Nightingale Room used for literary events.

items.name: Heath Info Hut, Parliament Hill
items.description: Fixed Heath Hands information hut at Parliament Hill, open on advertised drop-in days for maps, nature sheets and local activity information.

items.name: Freud Museum London
items.description: Sigmund and Anna Freud’s former home at 20 Maresfield Gardens, with collections and exhibitions. Published admission charges and opening hours apply.

items.name: Guildhall Art Gallery
items.description: Free public gallery beside Guildhall Yard, with access to London’s Roman Amphitheatre and regular introductory tours.

items.name: National Gallery
items.description: Public art museum on Trafalgar Square, with free collection admission and scheduled guided tours.

items.name: Parliament Hill Café
items.description: Fixed café on Hampstead Heath and the meeting point for Heath Hands’ gentler and medium health walks.

items.name: The Hive, Hampstead Heath
items.description: Heath Hands’ fixed activity and volunteering venue by Nassington Road, used for gardening and community sessions.

items.name: Kenwood Dairy
items.description: Historic Dairy buildings at Kenwood, home to Heath Hands and its Nature Interpretation Centre. Public access on advertised open days.
